A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SpiderGPT study. Their main texts, figures, tables and Appendix A are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and revised evaluation protocols.

before.justification: v1 reports original computational sequence-generation, mechanical-property prediction, motif-correlation and ablation results in Sections 4–5.

after.justification: v2 reports original computational results, including revised property predictions, a SilkomeGPT comparison and distribution tests, alongside retained generation and ablation experiments.

M1.justification: The distilled SpiderGPT architecture, three-stage pipeline, LoRA fine-tuning, causal language-modeling objective and task-token-conditioned bidirectional operation remain. Expanded conditioning-vector notation and implementation explanations do not establish a new method component; revised training settings are assessed under E3.

E1.justification: Both versions use approximately 100,000 spider proteins, 6,000 MaSp repeats, 592 property-labeled sequences from 293 species and the same 11,000-sequence BLAST search space. Generation and property-prediction tasks remain unchanged. Revised sample counts, partitions and input preprocessing change the protocol rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds SilkomeGPT as an evaluated mechanical-property prediction baseline in Table 1; v1 only discussed the corresponding prior work. This introduces a direct comparison with another silk-design model for the principal prediction task. The existing ProtGPT2 efficiency comparison and omitted-Level-1 variant remain.

E3.justification: The 572-training/20-test split becomes five selected validation folds from a 16-part partition, with 555 training and 37 held-out sequences per run and 185 evaluated records. Stage 3's reported learning rate changes from 1e-4 to 1e-5 and its training limit from five to ten epochs. Unconditional generation increases from 200 to 500 sequences. v2 also adds Spearman correlation and R2 metrics and uses unprocessed sequences for both models in the new baseline comparison.

E4.justification: Figure 7(b) adds analysis of whether predicted and reference mechanical-property distributions agree, using density plots and Kolmogorov–Smirnov tests. The existing property-prediction ablation gains rank-correlation and R2 diagnostics. The distillation and sequence-generation ablations remain, including the 68% non-repeat-generation finding.

E5.justification: v2 explicitly reports five independently trained fold-specific models instead of the single-split evaluation described in v1. Figure 7(b) introduces goodness-of-fit p-values and distribution means and standard deviations. These substantially expand statistical reporting, although seeds, confidence intervals and numerical variability across folds are still not reported.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the 20-instance results, including Pearson r=0.3911 and MAE=0.0587, with 185-instance results of r=0.8884 and MAE=0.0861 under revised settings. These are not same-setting performance gains. New SilkomeGPT entries report r=0.8349 and MAE=0.0963. Table 3's ablation results and Figures 4, 5 and 7 also change; for example, the YGQGG-count/toughness correlation changes from 0.198 to 0.228.

T1.justification: The new dataset and task notation formalizes previously described data and mappings without introducing substantive theory. Motif definitions and the KL-divergence formula remain equivalent. Removing the standard molecular-weight formula and adding discussion of the standard R2 relationship concern metric explanation, not new assumptions, proofs or theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contributions: a compact, repeat-specific model for property-conditioned sequence generation and mechanical-property prediction, supported by computational biological-plausibility checks. Updated evaluation descriptions do not redefine these claims, and experimental synthesis remains future work.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly qualifies sequence–property matching as non-one-to-one and its comparison as qualitative in Section 5.1.1. It discusses possible terminal–repeat interactions, acknowledges SilkomeGPT's exposure to the evaluation instances during training, and interprets negative ablation R2 as worse than a mean predictor. Appendix A.2 now explains the biological rationale for the selected physicochemical attributes.

D1.justification: v2 adds a Software and Data section reporting an inference repository containing scripts, configurations, usage instructions and datasets; v1 supplied no implementation repository. It also newly documents PEFT usage, unchanged biases, subtype-level deduplication, Stage 3 tokenization and fold-specific exports. Conversely, Appendix A.2 removes the explicit molecular-weight calculation in favor of evaluation rationale.

R1.justification: v2 adds supporting literature on terminal-domain biology and generative protein design, including ProteinGAN, ProGen2 and RFdiffusion, plus an audio post-training analogy and references for evaluation rationale. The central positioning against full-length spidroin design by Lu et al. remains. The Lehninger reference disappears with the molecular-weight calculation discussion.

P1.justification: Substantial passages in the literature review, distillation and fine-tuning descriptions, and prediction discussion are rewritten or reorganized, including expanded explanations of existing components. Appendix A.2 is repurposed, the Impact Statement is removed, and Software and Data and Acknowledgments sections are added. Citations also switch from numerical to author–date style.

P2.justification: The paper adopts TMLR typography, a different title/author arrangement, running headers and extensive float relocation. Figure 2 gains LoRA/cross-validation labels, Figures 4 and 5 are redrawn, and Figure 7 expands from scatter plots to combined scatter and density panels. Table 1 gains a baseline column and additional metrics; Table 3 also expands. Several other figures retain their original content.

improvement.justification: The direct SilkomeGPT comparison, specified evaluation partitions, clearer qualifications and code/data access information make v2 easier to assess and reproduce. However, the expanded evaluation lacks reported variability across folds, and new reporting inconsistencies limit confidence: Figure 3 is unchanged despite the stated increase from 200 to 500 generated sequences, while the introduction retains cosine similarity 0.9465 despite Table 1 reporting 0.9827. The documentation and comparison gains support a limited net improvement.
